extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the PARI/GP system (computational number theorists, mathematicians writing code with PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP functions dealing with modular-symbol polygons, q-expansions, p-adic lifts, Hecke-splitting, and plotting APIs (high-level and low-level). It specifies function semantics, flags, preconditions, outputs and usage examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspolygon: convex hull selection and edge-pairing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct the convex hull polygon for Γ0(N) acting on the Poincaré half-plane by selecting edges in E satisfying pairing conditions: include edges e with e = e* or e* = e when the pairing matrix γ_e has order 2; include the edges (r,t) and (t,s) when e=(r,s)∈E satisfies e = e* and γ_e has order 3 and the triangle (r,t,s) is the image of (0, exp(2iπ/3), ∞) by some element of PSL2(Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determines the polygon used to represent the quotient surface; the precise inclusion rules are necessary to get correct fundamental polygons and later topological/homological information (e.g., symplectic basis of H1). Examples in the manual show usage via mspolygon(...) calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspolygon: flag bit 1 — normalized vs unimodular polygon
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary flag bit 1: if set, return a normalized hyperbolic polygon; otherwise return a polygon whose edges are unimodular matrices (determinant 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A normalized polygon is defined so that distance d(a,a*) between an edge and its involution image is < 2 (with equality iff a is linked with another edge). Vertices of edges with d(a,a*) ≠ 1 are all equivalent to 0 mod Γ0(N). External vertices of aa* with d(a,a*)=1 are equivalent to 0; internal vertices a∩a* together with 0 form representatives of cusps. Normalized polygons give a symplectic basis for H1(X0(N), Z). Examples show difference: normalized polygon may have non-unimodular edge matrices (matdet values >1).

rubrics_metrics.name: mspolygon: normalized polygon topology consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Properties of normalized polygon relate to genus, elliptic points and cusps: genus equals the number of aba* b* blocks; elliptic points correspond to fixed points in A; number of cusps equals number of aa* blocks plus 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the polygon structure (ordering of edges A) to deduce genus and cusp data; e.g., X0(14) example: polygon form (a1,a1*,a2,a2*,a3,a3*,a4,a5,a4*,a5*) shows genus 1, no elliptic points, and 4 cusps. Paths corresponding to edges projecting to loops may form a symplectic homology basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspolygon: flag bit 2 — generate LaTeX/TikZ graphical representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary flag bit 2: add graphical representations (in LaTeX form) for the hyperbolic polygon in Poincaré's half-space and the involution a→a* of the Farey symbol; returned character strings can be written to file and included in a LaTeX document that uses \usepackage{tikz}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows writing D1 and D2 outputs to a .tex file by concatenation inside a document skeleton. Useful for including polygon pictures in papers or notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspolygon: unimodular vs normalized edge determinants
rubrics_metrics.description: When mspolygon is called without normalization, the edge matrices may all be unimodular (determinant 1). When requesting normalization, edges may no longer be unimodular and their determinants can be >1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual gives examples: mspolygon(15) returns all matdet = 1; mspolygon(15,1) returns determinants [1,1,1,1,2,2,47,11,47,11] illustrating that normalization can introduce non-unimodular edge matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: msqexpansion: produce Fourier coefficients of normalized newform
rubrics_metrics.description: msqexpansion(M, projH, {B=seriesprecision}) returns Fourier coefficients a_n for n ≤ B of the normalized newform corresponding to projector projH on a Hecke-simple subspace of a full modular symbol space M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If B omitted, uses seriesprecision. The function uses a naive O(B^2 d^3) algorithm where d = O(kN) is dimension of Mk(Γ0(N)). Examples demonstrate agreement with ellan for elliptic curve labels. Use msqexpansion(M, s, B) directly if s is a Hecke eigenvector (shortcut).

rubrics_metrics.name: msqexpansion: computational complexity note
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic complexity for msqexpansion is O(B^2 d^3) where d is the dimension of Mk(Γ0(N)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of potential high cost for large B or large dimension d; choose B (seriesprecision) appropriately and prefer other optimized workflows if available for large computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: msqexpansion: shortcut for Hecke eigenvector
rubrics_metrics.description: msqexpansion(M, s, B) is a shortcut available when s is a modular symbol which is a Hecke eigenvector: you may pass the symbol directly instead of a projector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show obtaining symbols from ellinit/ msfromell and calling msqexpansion on sp or sm to get q-expansion coefficients directly for +/− eigenspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: mssplit: split Hecke-stable subspace into Hecke-simple subspaces
rubrics_metrics.description: mssplit(M, {H}, {dimlim}) splits a Hecke-stable subspace H (or the full new subspace if omitted) into Hecke-simple subspaces; if dimlim is positive, restrict to subspaces of dimension ≤ dimlim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each returned subspace is represented by a structure whose first component is an integer matrix whose columns form a Q-basis of the subspace, enabling fast projection and restriction of linear operators. The manual demonstrates splitting M_8(Γ0(11))^+ into two pieces and computing associated newform polynomials and Fourier coefficients. Use dimlim to limit search to small-degree subspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: mssplit: interpretation of outputs (number fields/newforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: To a Hecke-simple subspace corresponds an orbit of normalized newforms defined over a number field; mssplit returns data enabling extraction of field-defining polynomials and representative Fourier coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example prints polynomials 'mod' (field-defining) and the first few Fourier coefficients; use lift(...) on returned q-expansion to obtain full coefficient vectors in a chosen polynomial basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: msstar: *-involution matrix (complex conjugation)
rubrics_metrics.description: msstar(M, {H}) returns the matrix of the * involution induced by complex conjugation acting on the (stable) subspace H (or M if omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property check: w = msstar(M) should satisfy w^2 == 1. Use to separate ± eigenspaces under complex conjugation or for symmetry checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: mstooms: lift classical eigen-symbol to p-adic overconvergent symbol (Pollack–Stevens)
rubrics_metrics.description: mstooms(Mp, phi) lifts a classical eigen symbol φ to a p-adic distribution-valued overconvergent modular symbol Φ given Mp from mspadicinit. Preconditions: φ belongs to modular symbols of level N (vp(N) ≤ 1), weight k, and is an eigenvector for TN(p) with non-zero eigenvalue a_p. Let N0 = lcm(N,p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise output depends on whether p divides N and on v_p(a_p): - If p ∤ N and a_p divisible by p, returns lift Φ of (φ, φ|_k V_p) such that T_{N0}(p)Φ = C_p Φ with C_p = [a_p, p^{k-1}; -1, 0]. - If p ∤ N and a_p is a p-unit, returns lift Φ of φ - α^{-1} φ|_k V_p which is eigenvector for T_{N0}(p) of unit eigenvalue where α^2 - a_p α + p^{k-1} = 0. Resulting overconvergent eigensymbol can be used with mspadicmoments, mspadicL or mspadicseries. The function will signal incorrect type/error when v_p(a_p) exceeds the mspadicinit flag (example error shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: mstooms: usage pattern and error conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical workflow: obtain φ from classical Hecke operator kernel, initialize Mp = mspadicinit(M,p,prec, flag), call mstooms(Mp,φ) to get PHI, then call mspadicmoments(Mp,PHI) and mspadicL(mu) to compute p-adic L-values/series. Error arises if φ is non-ordinary and the mspadicinit flag is incompatible (v_p(a_p) > mspadicinit flag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates need to set appropriate mspadicinit flag to allow non-ordinary symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plotting functions: three categories and general semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI plotting functions are organized into: high-level plotting functions (ploth*), low-level rectplot functions (plot*), and functions for producing PostScript/SVG output (plotexport/plothexport/plothrawexport).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-level functions manage 16 virtual rectwindows that must be initialized via plotinit; a virtual cursor is attached to each window and plotdraw displays/exports contents. High-level functions provide simple interfaces for common plots and may fork a child process so the gp session remains usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual rectwindows, virtual cursor, and plotdraw behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 16 virtual windows numbered 0..15; they must be initialized with plotinit (size). A virtual cursor (initialized at [0,0]) is attached to each window and its current value can be obtained via plotcursor. Only portions of objects inside the window are drawn (except polygons and strings drawn entirely). plotdraw physically draws windows, forking a child process so gp session is not blocked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To erase a window use plotkill. You cannot partially erase a window: you must reinitialize and redraw content to retain parts. Use plotscale to control coordinate scaling for portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: parploth/ploth/ploth* high-precision plotting: precision and n parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: parploth and ploth are high-precision plotting functions that may evaluate the plotted expression thousands of times; the function returns bounding box [xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax]. Parameter n controls number of reference points (0 uses defaults: 1000 general, 1500 parametric, 8 recursive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many evaluations are performed, keep gp precision minimal (e.g., 9) before calling. Use appropriate n; defaults are tuned but can be adjusted for performance/accuracy tradeoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: parploth/ploth: binary flag bits and their meanings (display options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary digits of flag control plotting modes and display options. Key bits: 1 = Parametric, 2 = Recursive. Other bits: 4 = no Rescale, 8 = no X axis, 16 = no Y axis, 32 = no Frame, 64 = no Lines (only points), 128 = Points too (lines+points), 256 = Splines, 512 = no X ticks, 1024 = no Y ticks, 2048 = Same ticks (equal tick lengths), 4096 = Complex (treat expr items as complex encoding coordinates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parametric (1) requires expr to be a vector of even length; recursive (2) performs adaptive subdivision and can be faster but risks producing incorrect polygonal approximations if unlucky or parameters are poorly chosen (e.g., avoid plotting recursively odd functions on symmetric intervals). Use no Rescale (4) with plotscale when combining multiple plots to avoid distortion. Examples illustrate combinations and anti-patterns (e.g., recursive plot odd functions, distorted circle without no Rescale).

rubrics_metrics.name: parploth/ploth: parametric and recursive modes (use-cases and warnings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parametric mode (flag bit 1) draws curves from successive pairs of components in expr; recursive mode (bit 2) adaptively refines intervals by inserting midpoints when local linear approximation is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recursive plotting is fast and often more precise but can fail for poorly chosen n or symmetric odd functions (may produce polygon that misrepresents the curve). Recommendation: try plotting with slightly different parameters to ensure correct shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotexport/plothexport/plothrawexport: PostScript/SVG export semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: plotexport, plothexport and plothrawexport convert plots/rectwindows or high-precision plots into character strings in 'ps' or 'svg' format which can be written to files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exports are available even without a graphical driver. Example shows obtaining an SVG string and write("graph.svg", s). When display has no sense (SVG/PS), plothsizes returns zero display width/height.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcolor: color input formats and return value
rubrics_metrics.description: plotcolor(w, c) sets default color for rectwindow w and returns RGB vector [R,G,B]. Acceptable c: a 3-vector of integers [R,G,B] (0..255), a string color name supported by rgb.txt, a hex #RRGGBB string, or an integer index into the graphcolormap (factory defaults map 1=black,2=blue,3=violetred,4=red,5=green,6=grey,7=gainsborough).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: plotcolor(0, "turquoise") returns [64,224,208]; plotcolor(0,2) returns [0,0,255]. Use appropriate format for portability across drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotinit and plotscale: initialization and portable coordinate setup
rubrics_metrics.description: plotinit(w, {x}, {y}, {flag=0}) initializes rectwindow w and sets virtual cursor to (0,0); x and y are width/height in pixels unless flag≠0 (fractions of device size). Use plothsizes() to query device dimensions and then plotscale to set a portable coordinate system (example uses [0,1000]×[0,1000]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plotinit destroys previous rect objects in the window. To reuse a window, call plotinit again. Use plotscale to avoid device-dependent distortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotdraw: drawing layout and coordinate convention for multiple windows
rubrics_metrics.description: plotdraw(w, {flag=0}) physically draws rectwindow w or a list [w1,x1,y1,w2,x2,y2,...] placing windows with upper-left corners at given positions; if flag=0, x1,y1 are fractions of current output device size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlapping regions are drawn twice and windows are considered transparent. Use plotexport to avoid forking or to obtain file output.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotcopy: copying windows with offsets and corner conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: plotcopy(sourcew, destw, dx, dy, {flag=0}) copies contents of rectwindow sourcew to destw with offset (dx,dy). If flag bit 1 set, dx and dy are fractions of output device size; otherwise they are pixels. The reference corner for dx,dy is northwest if other bits vanish; other bits alter to southwest, southeast, northeast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to compose complex images from smaller rectwindows; be careful about flag bits indicating units and corner reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotlines/plotpoints/plotbox: primitive drawing semantics and cursor behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: plotlines(w,X,Y,{flag=0}) draws polygon with vertex coordinates in X,Y; if X,Y scalars a single segment from current cursor to (X,Y) is drawn and cursor moves. plotpoints draws points inside w, moving cursor if scalars given. plotbox draws rectangle from current cursor to (x2,y2) outline; if filled=1, fills it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: plotlines draws entire polygon (not clipped) for simplicity; to draw from an arbitrary start use plotmove before plotlines. If few points are drawn they may be hard to see; use filled boxes (plotrbox) to simulate thick points. Examples show differences and suggested sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotstring: text justification bits and insertion gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: plotstring(w, x, {flags=0}) draws string x at current cursor position. Bits 1 and 2 regulate horizontal alignment (left=0, center=1, right=2). Bits 4 and 8 regulate vertical alignment (bottom=0, v-center=4, top=8). Bits 16 and 32 insert small horizontal/vertical gaps between point and string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bit combinations to control exact string placement; see tutorial for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-level rect-operations relative to virtual cursor (plotr* functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions plotrbox, plotrline, plotrmove, plotrpoint etc. operate relative to the current virtual cursor: e.g., plotrbox(w, dx, dy, {filled}) draws rectangle from (x1,y1) to (x1+dx,y1+dy) where (x1,y1) is cursor, leaving cursor unchanged; plotrline draws segment from cursor to cursor+(dx,dy) and moves cursor; plotrpoint draws point at cursor+(dx,dy) and moves cursor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These primitives enable building drawings incrementally using relative coordinates; examples show building thick points and sequences of moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: plothraw/plothrawexport: plotting raw points with equal x/y scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: plothraw(X,Y,{flag=0}) plots points (X[i],Y[i]) in high precision; automatic positioning/scaling uses same scaling factor on x and y. If flag=1 join points. plothrawexport(fmt,X,Y,flag) returns exported 'ps' or 'svg' string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plothraw when preserving aspect ratio is important (equal scaling). Use export to save results for external viewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: plothsizes: query output window/display metrics and units
rubrics_metrics.description: plothsizes({flag=0}) returns 8-component vector: window width, height, tick sizes horizontal/vertical, char width/height, display width/height (display width/height are 0 for svg/ps). If flag=0 sizes are in pixels; otherwise they are fractions of screen size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plothsizes to write device-independent code (e.g., to set up full-size rectwindow and then plotscale to a fixed coordinate box).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecated/obsolete plotting functions: prefer new export APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions such as psdraw, psploth, psplothraw are obsolete; use plotexport/plothexport/plothrawexport instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid obsolete functions in new code; use the export routines which produce PS/SVG strings and are supported even without a graphical driver.
